samples.summary: Table-cell text still paints legacy `color: ''` through `??`, so the #728 stale-fillStyle bug survives inside tables
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:457` — `const runTextColor = defaultColorResolver(style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;` and `:564` — `ctx.fillStyle = defaultColorResolver(cellBlock.inlines[0]?.style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;`. Table blocks never go through `renderRun` (paint-layout skips `block.type === 'table'` at lines 221 and 277; table-renderer does its own `ctx.font`/`ctx.fillStyle`/`ctx.fillText` at 451-483 and the list-marker path at 558-565). `defaultColorResolver` returns strings verbatim (`packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:16`), so a stored `color: ''` yields `''`, `ctx.fillStyle = ''` is ignored by the canvas, and the run keeps whatever the previous pass set — the table content pass runs *after* the selection layer (see the comment at table-renderer.ts:471-474 and the explicit `ctx.fillStyle = focused ? Theme.selectionColor : ...` at :442). The task doc for this change explicitly declines a data migration (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:51-52), so already-saved `''` values are the intended coverage of the renderer guard — and text in tables is not covered. Fix belongs in table-renderer.ts:457/564 (`|| Theme.defaultColor`).

samples.summary: `underlineColor` in the same function still uses `??`, so an empty-string color can leak into `ctx.strokeStyle`
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:454 — `ctx.strokeStyle = resolveColor(style.underlineColor) ?? textColor;`. Same falsy-color hazard the diff fixed three lines up for `style.color`; a `''` here silently keeps the previous strokeStyle. Reachability is narrower (no toolbar writes `underlineColor`; only the PPTX importer sets it, packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:505), so the empty string would have to come from imported/legacy data.

samples.summary: A sibling colour-reset path still writes `""` instead of `undefined`, contradicting the convention this change establishes
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230 — `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })`. The diff's new rule is that clearing a colour means passing `undefined` so the store issues `removeStyleByPath` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163); this call instead persists an empty-string attribute in the CRDT. It happens to render as "no fill" because the cell-background painter guards with a truthiness check (packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:175-176), so it is cosmetic/consistency rather than a visible bug today, but it keeps seeding the invalid values the new renderer guards exist to tolerate.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The #728 guard uses `||` in the shared body painter (paint-layout.ts:389 for run text, paint-layout.ts:558 for list markers, with comments at 385-388 and 545-549 stating that a cleared color arrives as `''` and `ctx.fillStyle = ''` is ignored). Table blocks bypass that painter entirely: paint-layout.ts:167, :221 and :277 all skip `block.type === 'table'`. The table painter does its own text pass with `??`, which does not filter `''`: table-renderer.ts:457 (`defaultColorResolver(style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor`, consumed by ctx.fillStyle at :458 and strokeStyle at :489/:500) and table-renderer.ts:564 (list-marker fillStyle). `defaultColorResolver` passes strings through verbatim (model/color.ts:16), so a stored `color: ''` yields `''`. The stale-fillStyle is observable because the selection layer paints first: doc-canvas.ts:463 sets `Theme.selectionColor` before invoking renderTableContent at doc-canvas.ts:525, and table-renderer.ts:442/471-474 confirm the content pass follows the selection fill. No upstream guard normalizes `''` (no matches for `color === ''`/`color: ''` in packages/docs/src; serialize/json.ts does no color handling), and docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:51-52 explicitly declines a migration, making already-stored `''` the intended coverage of the renderer guard. This is the lens's core pattern: a new guard with an unguarded sibling paint path outside the diff.
